verdict.rationale: Gram documents first-party usage analytics. A dashboard shows total spend, agent sessions and tool-call counts; the GitHub README describes tracking AI usage across teams by tokens or cost with budgets and tool-effectiveness measurement; and tool logs record every tool call, filterable by attribute and tied to a named employee. Error analytics are not explicitly evidenced, and a per-server breakdown of call volume is only implied, so the story is not completely covered. Missing for 10: explicit error-rate or failure analytics, documented per-server and per-tool call-volume breakdowns for both consumed and published servers, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can see usage analytics for the servers and tools my org consumes or publishes — call volumes, users, errors, and cost

citations.quote: Track AI usage across teams and measure impact with either tokens or cost. Deep dive expensive sessions, create budgets and measure tool effectiveness.
the raw execution log for every tool call the platform observes across hosted MCP servers, tunneled and shadow MCP servers, skills, and local tools

The raw stream of tool executions across MCP servers, skills, and local tools, with trace expansion and attribute filters.
